title: The bus retires a ruled set of requests and their replies through its own door
intention: The bus retires, through its own owner-gated door, every request to a named device on named verbs together with the replies to them and their delivery receipts, and leaves a retirement record in the logging tree — first used to delete the 10,548 trouble-ticket rows Akien ruled must not exist.
why: Akien 2026-10-18: 'THERE SHOULD BE NO ROWS FOR TROUBLE TICKETS' and 'those wrong and bad things all deleted once it's fixed'. ee04bb869795 (PROVED 2026-10-19) moved every trouble reader off the bus, but the 10,548 rows it left (5,274 requests, 5,274 replies, ~791 MB of reply bodies) still stand, and the bus has no door to delete them.
traces_to: Law 6 (the bus owns bus_traffic, so only the bus's own gate deletes its rows) and Law 7 (the deletion is loud: a retirement record in the logging tree names what went); Akien's outline, bus entry: 'the database exists to queue undelivered messages while shims are brought online'; his rulings 2026-10-18 'THERE SHOULD BE NO ROWS FOR TROUBLE TICKETS' and 'those wrong and bad things all deleted once it's fixed' (ee04bb869795 made the fix, PROVED 2026-10-19).
how: A BusDevice method retire(addressee, verbs, why) that, in one transaction through db_domain's store.delete under owner 'bus', deletes the receipts of the matched envelopes, then the replies (reply_to IN the matched requests), then the requests, and appends one JSON line to log_path('cairn',0)/bus/retired.jsonl naming the why, the match, the counts per sender/addressee/verb and the date span. It refuses an empty verb list or a blank why, and leaves rows it does not match (the 354 trouble menu rows the base shim publishes) alone. Then it is run once over addressee 'trouble', verbs live/clears/clear/get/show, citing Akien 2026-10-18.
falsifier: Proof cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_a_ruled_retire_deletes_requests_and_replies.py over BusDevice.scratch(): post 3 requests to 'trouble' on verb 'live' plus their 3 replies (reply_to set) and receipts for all 6, 1 request on verb 'clears' plus reply, 1 menu row from trouble to trouble verb '', 2 rows between other devices; flush; then retire(addressee='trouble', verbs=['live','clears'], why='proof'). RED unless: (1) every matched request, reply and receipt is gone and count(to='trouble') reads only the menu row; (2) the menu row and both other-device rows still stand, and the total falls by exactly 8 envelopes; (3) the return value and the emitted 'retired' record both carry requests 4, replies 4, receipts 6 and the why; (4) retire with verbs=[] or why='' raises ValueError and deletes nothing; (5) a request still in the ring (posted, not flushed) is retired too, never resurrected by a later flush. Horizon: sealed green, and the hollow revert of bus.py reds teeth 1-5. Then live: the run over trouble leaves 0 matched rows and the emitted record's counts equal the before-minus-after difference.
builder_notes: Q: signature? A: BusDevice.retire(self, *, addressee: str, verbs: list[str] | tuple[str, ...], why: str) -> dict. Q: refusals? A: raise ValueError before touching anything if verbs is empty, why is blank, or addressee is blank. Q: order? A: self.flush() first; then under self._lock drop from self._ring any envelope matched (addressee==addressee and verb in verbs) or whose reply_to is a matched id, and from self._ring_receipts any receipt naming one; then self._ensure(); one connection with autocommit False: collect request ids (SELECT id FROM table WHERE addressee=%s AND verb = ANY(%s)), reply ids (SELECT id WHERE reply_to = ANY(request ids)), delete receipts WHERE envelope = ANY(all ids) via store.delete(self._delivery_table, _BUS_OWNER, where='envelope = ANY(%s)', params=(ids,), conn=conn), then replies and requests via store.delete(self._table, _BUS_OWNER, where='id = ANY(%s)', ...); commit, rollback on any exception and re-raise. Q: return? A: {'requests': n, 'replies': n, 'receipts': n, 'addressee': ..., 'verbs': [...], 'why': ...} counting ring and table together. Q: record? A: self.emit('retired', pointer=addressee, values=<the return dict>). Q: proof shape? A: like test_a_read_takes_the_newest_n.py: BusDevice.scratch(), _tooth with PASS/FAIL lines, a composite tooth named in PROVES, subject bound at call time.
decisions: A method on the bus module, no bus verb or CLI, and the match is a named addressee + verbs + the replies naming those requests (menu rows and other devices' rows untouched) — CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'

decisions.text: THE BUILD, exactly: in cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py add BusDevice.retire(self, *, addressee, verbs, why) -> dict. Refuse (ValueError, nothing touched) a blank addressee, empty verbs or blank why. self.flush(); under self._lock drop matched envelopes (addressee and verb in verbs), envelopes whose reply_to is a matched id, and receipts naming any of them from self._ring / self._ring_receipts, counting them; self._ensure(); one connection, autocommit False: request ids = SELECT id WHERE addressee=%s AND verb = ANY(%s); reply ids = SELECT id WHERE reply_to = ANY(request ids); store.delete the receipts (envelope = ANY(all ids)) from self._delivery_table, then the replies and requests (id = ANY(ids)) from self._table, all under _BUS_OWNER with conn=conn; commit, or rollback and re-raise. Return {'requests','replies','receipts','addressee','verbs','why'} (ring + table counts), and self.emit('retired', pointer=addressee, values=<that dict>). Proof at cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_a_ruled_retire_deletes_requests_and_replies.py per the falsifier. Then run it once over addressee 'trouble', verbs live/clears/clear/get/show, why citing Akien 2026-10-18, and record the counts in the verdict. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'

_BUS_OWNER already stands at module level in cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py:108 as _BUS_OWNER = "bus" (measured 2026-10-19 by grep); the build uses it as is and defines nothing new. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'

The live run happens after the PROVEME crossing and before verdict.write_verdict. A scratchpad script (live_retire.py, run as PYTHONPATH=. python3 from the cairn root, full env) builds BusDevice() over the default table bus_traffic and calls retire(addressee='trouble', verbs=['live','clears','clear','get','show'], why='Akien 2026-10-18: THERE SHOULD BE NO ROWS FOR TROUBLE TICKETS; those wrong and bad things all deleted once it is fixed'). Before and after the call it counts, through store.query, every bus_traffic row, the rows to trouble on those verbs, the rows whose reply_to names one of them, every bus_traffic_delivery row, and the trouble->trouble announce menu rows. It writes the before, the after and the returned dict to one JSON file in the scratchpad, and the verdict's criterion-2 evidence quotes them. The script's fresh BusDevice has an empty ring. The live bus process's ring holds no trouble row: none was posted after 2026-10-18T21:38:27 and every beat flushes the ring. So the table delete is the whole set. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'
